subject: Chemistry
subtopic: Reduction of Nitriles to Primary Amines
stem:
Select the reagents that reduce nitriles to primary amines.

A. (i) LiAlH\(_4\); (ii) H\(_2\)O
B. Sn + HCl
C. H\(_2\)/Ni
D. Na(Hg)/C\(_2\)H\(_5\)OH
E. Br\(_2\)/aq. NaOH

Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
solution:
\(\text{R–CN} \xrightarrow{\text{Na(Hg)/C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH}} \text{R–CH}_2\text{–NH}_2\)
\(\text{R–CN} \xrightarrow{\text{(i) LiAlH}_4,\ \text{(ii) H}_2\text{O}} \text{R–CH}_2\text{–NH}_2\)
\(\text{R–CN} \xrightarrow{\text{Sn+HCl}} \text{R–CHO}\)
\(\text{R–CN} \xrightarrow{\text{H}_2\text{/Ni}} \text{R–CH}_2\text{–NH}_2\)
So A, C and D reduce nitriles to primary amines.

subject: Chemistry
stem:
Consider the following reaction :
\[2A(g) + B(g) \rightarrow 2D(g)\]
\(\Delta U^\ominus = -10\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1}\) and \(\Delta S^\ominus = -44\ \text{JK}^{-1}\) at 298 K.
Identify the correct option with \(\Delta G^\ominus\) for the reaction and spontaneity of the reaction at 298 K.
(Given : R = 8.31 J mol\(^{-1}\) K\(^{-1}\))
solution:
\(2A(g)+B(g) \rightarrow 2D(g)\)
\(\Delta U^\circ = -10\) kJ/mol, \(\Delta S^\circ = -44\) J/K
\(\Delta H^\circ = \Delta U^\circ + \Delta n_g RT\)
\(\Delta H^\circ = -10 - \dfrac{1 \times 298 \times 8.31}{1000} = -10 - 2.48 = -12.48\) kJ/mol
\(\Delta G^\circ = \Delta H^\circ - T\Delta S^\circ = -12.48 - \dfrac{298 \times (-44)}{1000} = -12.48 + 13.112 = +0.632\) kJ/mol
Since \(\Delta G^\circ\) is positive, the given process is non-spontaneous.

subject: Chemistry
stem:
In a qualitative analysis, Bi\(^{3+}\) is detected by appearance of precipitate of BiO(OH)(s). Calculate pH when the following equilibrium exists at 298 K.
\[\text{BiO(OH)(s)} \rightleftharpoons \text{BiO}^{+}(aq) + \text{OH}^{-}(aq),\ K = 4 \times 10^{-10}\]
(Given : log2 = 0.3010)
solution:
\(\text{BiO(OH)(s)} \rightleftharpoons \text{BiO}^{+}(aq) + \text{OH}^{-}(aq)\), both \(= s\)
\(K = \dfrac{[\text{BiO}^{+}][\text{OH}^{-}]}{1} = s \times s = s^2\)
\(s = \sqrt{K} = \sqrt{4 \times 10^{-10}} = 2 \times 10^{-5}\) M
\([\text{H}^{+}] = \dfrac{K_w}{[\text{OH}^{-}]} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 10^{-9}\), pH \(= -\log[\text{H}^{+}] = 9 + \log 2 = 9.301\)

stem: The correct statement with regard to the secondary structure of DNA/RNA is
options: RNA possesses a single strand helix structure and contains thymine as one of the four bases
DNA possesses a double strand helix structure and contains thymine as one of the four bases
RNA possesses a double strand helix structure and contains uracil as one of the four bases
DNA possesses a single strand helix structure and contains uracil as one of the four bases
solution: RNA is typically single stranded but it contains uracil, not thymine. DNA secondary structure has a double strand helix consisting of two polynucleotide chains. Its four nitrogenous bases are adenine (A), guanine (G), cytosine (C) and thymine (T).

subject: Chemistry
stem: A bulb is rated at 150 watt, converting 8% energy into light. If energy of one photon is \(4.42 \times 10^{-19}\) J, how many photons are emitted by the bulb per second?
solution:
Energy = Power \(\times\) time = 150 watt \(\times\) 1 s = 150 J
Energy converted to light \(= \dfrac{150 \times 8}{100} = 12\) J
E = nh\(\nu\), energy of one photon \(= 4.42 \times 10^{-19}\)
n = number of photons \(= \dfrac{E}{h\nu} = \dfrac{12}{4.42 \times 10^{-19}} = 2.715 \times 10^{19}\)

subject: Chemistry
stem:
Compound P (C\(_8\)H\(_8\)O) gives a red orange precipitate with 2,4-DNP reagent and it does not reduce Fehling's reagent. On drastic oxidation with chromic acid, P gives an aromatic product Q that produces effervescence on treating with aq. NaHCO\(_3\). Compounds P and Q, respectively, are :
(1) P = acetophenone (C\(_6\)H\(_5\)COCH\(_3\)); Q = phenylglyoxylic acid (C\(_6\)H\(_5\)COCOOH)
(2) P = 4-methylbenzaldehyde (p-CH\(_3\)-C\(_6\)H\(_4\)-CHO); Q = 4-methylbenzoic acid (p-CH\(_3\)-C\(_6\)H\(_4\)-COOH)
(3) P = 4-methylbenzaldehyde (p-CH\(_3\)-C\(_6\)H\(_4\)-CHO); Q = terephthalic acid (HOOC-C\(_6\)H\(_4\)-COOH)
(4) P = acetophenone (C\(_6\)H\(_5\)COCH\(_3\)); Q = benzoic acid (C\(_6\)H\(_5\)COOH)
solution:
Degree of unsaturation \(= (8+1) - \dfrac{8}{2} = 9 - 4 = 5\).
Since oxidation is under drastic condition, it must be a ketone.
P = acetophenone (C\(_6\)H\(_5\)COCH\(_3\)) gives positive 2,4-DNP test.
Chromic acid under drastic condition oxidises P to benzoic acid (C\(_6\)H\(_5\)COOH = Q), which with NaHCO\(_3\) gives C\(_6\)H\(_5\)COONa + H\(_2\)O + CO\(_2\)\(\uparrow\).
Official key given as (3 or 4).

stem:
The number of hydrogen atoms present in 5.4 g of urea is:
(Given: Molar mass of urea : 60 g mol\(^{-1}\); N\(_A\) : \(6.022 \times 10^{23}\) particles mol\(^{-1}\))
solution:
Structure of urea : H\(_2\)N–CO–NH\(_2\) (4 hydrogen atoms per molecule).
Mole of urea \(= \dfrac{5.4}{60} = 0.09\)
Number of hydrogen atoms \(= 0.09 \times 4 \times 6.022 \times 10^{23} = 2.1679 \times 10^{23} \approx 2.168 \times 10^{23}\)

subject: Chemistry
stem: Identify the incorrect statement from the following:
options: Nitrogen can form p\(\pi\)-p\(\pi\) multiple bonds with itself.
P(C\(_2\)H\(_5\))\(_3\) and As(C\(_6\)H\(_5\))\(_3\) form d\(\pi\)-d\(\pi\) bond with transition metals.
Phosphorus, arsenic and antimony show catenation property.
Nitrogen can form d\(\pi\)-p\(\pi\) bond with oxygen.
solution: Both nitrogen and oxygen do not contain d-orbitals so it cannot form d\(\pi\)-p\(\pi\) bond. Phosphorus and arsenic can form d\(\pi\)-d\(\pi\) bond with transition metals since both have vacant d-orbitals. Phosphorus, arsenic and antimony show catenation property. Hence statement (4) is incorrect.

chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
stem: The correct order of increasing metallic character of Na, Be, P, Mg and Si is
solution:
On moving left to right in a period, metallic character decreases, and on moving top to bottom in a group, metallic character increases. So the correct order of increasing metallic character is P < Si < Be < Mg < Na.
Electronegativity \(\propto \dfrac{1}{\text{Metallic character}}\). Electronegativity (Pauling scale): Na 0.9, Mg 1.2, Be 1.5, Si 1.8, P 2.1.

subject: Chemistry
stem:
Identify the correct statements :
(A) The molality of 2.5 g of ethanoic acid (Molar mass : 60 g mol\(^{-1}\)) in 75 g of benzene solution is 0.556 m.
(B) The molarity of a solution containing 5 g of NaOH (molar mass : 40 g mol\(^{-1}\)) in 450 mL of solution is 0.278 M at 298 K.
(C) Aquatic species are more comfortable in cold water.
(D) The solubility of gas increases with decrease in pressure.
(E) For a binary mixture of A and B, the number of moles of A and B are n\(_A\) and n\(_B\) respectively. The mole fraction of B will be \(x_B = \dfrac{n_A}{n_A + n_B}\).

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
solution:
(A) Molality \(= \dfrac{2.5}{60} \times \dfrac{1000}{75} = 0.556\) molal (correct)
(B) Molarity \(= \dfrac{5}{40} \times \dfrac{1000}{450} = 0.278\) M (correct)
(C) Aquatic species are more comfortable in cold water since Henry's law K\(_H \propto\) Temp \(\propto \dfrac{1}{\text{solubility}}\) (correct)
(D) According to Henry's Law, P = K\(_H\)X, P \(\propto\) solubility, so as P increases solubility increases (statement D wrong).
(E) \(x_B = \dfrac{n_B}{n_A + n_B}\) (statement E wrong).
So A, B and C are correct.

stem: At a certain temperature, T (K), during a process, 500 J is absorbed by the system and work of 200 J is done by the system. Then change in internal energy of the system is :
solution:
From first law of thermodynamics: \(\Delta U = q + w\)
q = +500 J (absorbed), w = -200 J (work done by system)
\(\Delta U = 500 - 200 = 300\) J

stem: At 298 K, a certain buffer solution contains equal concentrations of X\(^-\) and HX, K\(_b\) for X\(^-\) is 10\(^{-10}\). What is the pH of this buffer solution?
solution:
\(\text{HX} \rightleftharpoons \text{H}^+ + \text{X}^-\); K\(_a \times\) K\(_b\) = K\(_w\)
\(K_a = \dfrac{K_w}{K_b} = \dfrac{10^{-14}}{10^{-10}} = 10^{-4}\)
pH = pK\(_a\) + log\(\dfrac{[\text{X}^-]}{[\text{HX}]}\). Given [X\(^-\)] = [HX], pH = 4 + log(1) = 4 + 0 = 4

stem: The calculated 'spin-only' magnetic moment of Ti\(^{2+}\) (3d\(^2\)) is :
solution:
Spin only magnetic moment \(\mu = \sqrt{n(n+2)}\) B.M., where n = number of unpaired electrons.
Electronic configuration of Ti\(^{2+}\) \(\Rightarrow\) [Ar]4s\(^0\)3d\(^2\), so n = 2.
\(\mu = \sqrt{2 \times 4} = 2.84\) BM

subject: Chemistry
stem: Identify the incorrect statement from the following:
options: Carbon has the ability to form p\(\pi\)-p\(\pi\) multiple bond with itself.
ECl\(_3\) (E = B and Al) is a monomer when E = B and a dimer when E = Al.
The order of catenation property of Group 14 elements is C >> Si > Ge \(\approx\) Sn.
solution:
(1) C can form p\(\pi\)-p\(\pi\) multiple bond with itself (C=C and C\(\equiv\)C). (correct)
(2) BCl\(_3\) does not form dimer; AlCl\(_3\) can form dimer in Al\(_2\)Cl\(_6\). (correct)
(3) Catenation property of group 14: C >> Si > Ge \(\approx\) Sn. (correct)
(4) Oxygen exhibits oxidation state of 0 in O\(_2\), \(-2\) in oxides, \(-1\) in peroxides. So this statement is incorrect.

subject: Chemistry
stem:
The correct formal charges on oxygen atoms numbered 2, 1 and 3 respectively are :
(Structure of ozone O\(_3\): central oxygen labelled 1 is double-bonded to oxygen labelled 2 and single-bonded to oxygen labelled 3.)
solution:
Formal charge = Valence electrons (V) \(- \dfrac{1}{2}\)(shared electrons, S) \(-\) (non-bonding electrons, L).
Formal charge on 2nd oxygen atom \(= 6 - \dfrac{1}{2}(4) - 4 = 0\)
Formal charge on 1st oxygen atom \(= 6 - \dfrac{1}{2}(6) - 2 = +1\)
Formal charge on 3rd oxygen atom \(= 6 - \dfrac{1}{2}(2) - 6 = -1\)
So for oxygen 2, 1, 3 respectively: 0, +1, -1

subject: Chemistry
stem: Phenolphthalein is used as an indicator for the titration of sodium hydroxide solution against a standard solution of oxalic acid. The colour change that is observed at an alkaline pH close to the equivalence point during this titration is:
solution: Colour of phenolphthalein before the end point = colourless. Colour of phenolphthalein close to equivalence point (alkaline) = pink. Therefore colour change = colourless to pink.

subject: Chemistry
stem: When 1 dm\(^3\) of CO\(_2\) gas is passed over hot coke the volume of gaseous mixture after complete reaction at STP becomes 1.4 dm\(^3\). The composition of the gaseous mixture at STP is:
solution:
\(\text{CO}_2 + \text{C(s)} \rightarrow 2\text{CO}\)
Initial CO\(_2\) = 1, let x react: CO\(_2\) = (1-x), CO = 2x.
Total = (1-x) + 2x = 1 + x = 1.4, so x = 0.4 dm\(^3\).
Volume of CO\(_2\) = 1 - 0.4 = 0.6 dm\(^3\); Volume of CO = 2 \(\times\) 0.4 = 0.8 dm\(^3\).

subject: Chemistry
stem:
The major product Z formed in the following sequence of reactions is
\[\text{C}_2\text{H}_6 \xrightarrow[\text{UV light}]{\text{Cl}_2} X\ (\text{monochlorinated product}) \xrightarrow{\text{NH}_3} Y \xrightarrow[(\text{ii}) \text{H}_2\text{O}]{(\text{i}) \text{NaNO}_2/\text{HCl}} Z\]
solution:
\(\text{C}_2\text{H}_6 + \text{Cl}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{UV}} \text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{Cl (X)} + \text{HCl}\)
\(\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{Cl} \xrightarrow[-\text{HCl}]{\text{NH}_3} \text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{NH}_2 (Y)\)
\(\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{NH}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{NaNO}_2/\text{HCl}} [\text{C}_2\text{H}_5 + \text{N}_2^+\text{Cl}^-] \xrightarrow{\text{H}_2\text{O}} \text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH} (Z) + \text{N}_2 + \text{HCl}\)
So Z = C\(_2\)H\(_5\)OH

subject: Chemistry
stem:
Given below is an expression for the rate constant of a first-order reaction occurring at a certain temperature, T (K).
\[\ln k = 14.34 - \dfrac{1.25 \times 10^4}{T}\]
The energy of activation in kcal mol\(^{-1}\) for the reaction is :
(Given: k in s\(^{-1}\), R = 1.987 cal mol\(^{-1}\) K\(^{-1}\))
solution:
From Arrhenius equation: \(k = A e^{-E_a/RT}\), so \(\ln k = \ln A - \dfrac{E_a}{RT}\).
Comparing: \(\dfrac{E_a}{R} = 1.25 \times 10^4\)
\(E_a = 1.25 \times 10^4 \times 1.987 = 24.84\) kcal mol\(^{-1}\) (= 24840 cal mol\(^{-1}\))

subject: Chemistry
stem: Given below are certain reactions. Identify the reaction for which \(K_P \neq K_C\).
solution:
\(K_P = K_C (RT)^{\Delta n_g}\). For \(K_P = K_C\), \(\Delta n_g = 0\); for \(K_P \neq K_C\), \(\Delta n_g \neq 0\).
(1) \(\Delta n_g = 0\) (K\(_P\) = K\(_C\))
(2) \(\Delta n_g = 2 - 4 = -2\) (K\(_P \neq\) K\(_C\))
(3) \(\Delta n_g = 0\) (K\(_P\) = K\(_C\))
(4) \(\Delta n_g = 0\) (K\(_P\) = K\(_C\))
So reaction (2) has K\(_P \neq\) K\(_C\).

subject: Chemistry
chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
stem: Identify the incorrect statement from the following :
options: The largest and the smallest species among Mg, Mg\(^{2+}\), Al and Al\(^{3+}\) are Al and Mg\(^{2+}\) respectively.
The IUPAC name of the element with atomic number 107 is Unnilseptium.
The similarity in behaviour of Li with Mg is referred to as 'diagonal relationship'.
The oxidation state and covalency of Al in [AlCl(H\(_2\)O)\(_5\)]\(^{2+}\) are 3 and 6, respectively.
solution:
The largest species is Mg and the smallest one is Al\(^{3+}\) among Mg, Mg\(^{2+}\), Al and Al\(^{3+}\) (so statement (1) is incorrect).
Unnilseptium element has atomic number 107. Li and Mg are diagonally related and have similar properties. The oxidation state and covalency of Al in [AlCl(H\(_2\)O)\(_5\)]\(^{2+}\) are +3 and 6 respectively.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Mixture of chloroform and acetone forms a solution with negative deviation from Raoult's law due to :
options: Increase in escaping tendency of molecules of each component.
Formation of hydrogen bonding between acetone and chloroform
Stronger intermolecular forces between chloroform molecules than those between chloroform and acetone molecules.
solution: Acetone and chloroform show negative deviation from Raoult's law due to stronger H-bonding between acetone and chloroform mixture (C=O of acetone with H-CCl\(_3\) of chloroform). Hence escaping tendency decreases, vapour pressure decreases and boiling point increases.

subject: Chemistry
subtopic: Reactions of Benzene - Addition and Substitution
stem:
The number of chlorine atoms present in the organic products X and Y of the following reactions, respectively, are :
\[\text{Benzene} + 6\text{Cl}_2 \xrightarrow[\text{dark, cold}]{\text{Anhydr. AlCl}_3} X\]
\[\text{Benzene} + 3\text{Cl}_2 \xrightarrow[500\ \text{K}]{\text{UV}} Y\]
solution:
Benzene + 6Cl\(_2\) \(\xrightarrow[\text{dark, cold}]{\text{anhyd. AlCl}_3}\) hexachlorobenzene C\(_6\)Cl\(_6\) (substitution, X has 6 Cl atoms).
Benzene + 3Cl\(_2\) \(\xrightarrow[500\ \text{K}]{\text{UV}}\) benzene hexachloride C\(_6\)H\(_6\)Cl\(_6\) (BHC, addition, Y has 6 Cl atoms).
So X = 6 and Y = 6.
